title: Composition of hypercontractive inequalities
statement: Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $X:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$, let $p,r,q\\in[0,\\infty]$, and let $\\sigma,\\rho\\in\\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every $a,b\\in\\mathbb R$, the uniform $L^r$ norm of $a+\\sigma bX$ is at most the uniform $L^p$ norm of $a+bX$, and the uniform $L^q$ norm of $a+\\rho bX$ is at most the uniform $L^r$ norm of $a+bX$. Then for every $a,b\\in\\mathbb R$, the uniform $L^q$ norm of $a+\\rho\\sigma bX$ is at most the uniform $L^p$ norm of $a+bX$. Here the uniform norm at exponent $\\infty$ is the maximum absolute value on $\\Omega$.
hypotheses_covered: the stated affine norm inequality holds from exponent $p$ to $r$ with parameter $\\sigma$ for all real $a,b$
the stated affine norm inequality holds from exponent $r$ to $q$ with parameter $\\rho$ for all real $a,b$
